edge_explainer: The three screen fields that ranked this name are all wrong in the same direction, and correcting them removes the cheapness. (1) EV/EBIT 3.19x is really 6.2x: the vendor's EBIT of GBP64.0m equals statutory operating profit GBP45.0m plus the GBP18.4m bad-debt charge plus GBP0.6m non-recurring, added back as if unusual - but bad debt has run 3.1%/2.1%/2.6% of revenue in 2023/24/25 and is the structural cost of supplying SMEs. (2) Net cash of +31.7% of market cap is really +6.9%: the company's own CFO review states that GBP74m of the GBP106m cash balance is future liabilities - a GBP52.8m Renewable Obligation payment due to Ofgem in August 2026 (note 21) plus GBP21m of quarterly HMRC liabilities. (3) FCF yield 9.9% is really ~4.1%: GBP17.4m of the GBP36.3m operating cash inflow is simply the increase in the amount owed to Ofgem, and FY24's GBP72.1m was flattered by a one-off GBP49.8m release of commodity trading collateral when the Shell facility replaced the old one; management guides FY26 cash to decline on early ROC payment. Separately the frame fails: the stock is 8.2% below a 52-week high set on 2026-02-10 and 22.8% above a 298-day-old low, so it is not in a drawdown. Two verifications went the company's way - no defined-benefit pension (defined contribution only) and no capital commitments at all (note 26) - and the brief's hypothesis that hedge mark-to-market distorts EBIT is REFUTED: all forward commodity contracts are classified 'own use' and sit outside IFRS 9, so there is no fair-value movement in earnings. But that same classification hides a GBP395.6m forward commodity purchase book entirely off balance sheet - 4.0x equity - with the accounts stating explicitly that no sensitivity analysis is provided, and the classification resting on a management judgement about future customer demand. Business quality is genuine (meter points +49% to 131k, contract book GBP1.7bn, seventh consecutive period of meter growth) but unit economics are still deflating from crisis levels: gross margin 18.1% to 14.5% to 14.3%, net customer contribution 14.9% to 12.4% to 11.7%, adjusted EBITDA margin 9.5% to 7.6% to 7.2% and ~5.9% implied by FY26 guidance of flat profit on 21-25% revenue growth. Of GBP97.8m of net assets, GBP65.1m is unbilled management-estimated accrued income (provided at 3.7%) and GBP40.6m is capitalised customer-acquisition cost - together 108% of equity - so P/B 3.06 has no asset backing. The honesty prior is live: the October 2018 accounting collapse (the brief's '2016' date is wrong; 2016 was the IPO) was an accrued-income failure, the founder CEO remains in post, and the company's treasury has twice been the same-day buyer of insiders' stock, most recently GBP5.9m from the CEO at GBP19.06 on 13-Feb-2026, three days after the 52-week high and 33 days before guiding FY26 profit flat. Finally the Shell agreement that removes the collateral requirement grants Shell a fixed and floating charge over the whole operating business with covenants on profitability, net worth and liquidity, so a margin or bad-debt shock is not just an earnings event - it is a liquidity event against a GBP395.6m book backed by GBP32m of genuinely free cash. At 113bp of entry friction (0% AIM stamp plus a 225bp median touch) on $71k/day of tradeable size, none of this clears a default-REJECT bar.
